title: PIA 268
summary: PIA Flight 268 descended below cleared altitude during approach and crashed into the 8,250 ft Mahabharat Range mountain at Bhattedanda. The aircraft initiated each descent step too early, descending 1,300 feet below cleared altitude by the Sierra reporting point. Investigators determined pilot error as the primary cause, with contributions from poor visibility, lack of radar surveillance, and unclear approach plates.
probable_cause: Pilot error: the aircraft initiated each step of descent one step too early, approaching the Mahabharat Range at insufficient altitude. The lack of radar prevented controllers from warning of inappropriate altitude.

factors.evidence: The aircraft initiated each step of its descent one step too early.
The aircraft approached the Mahabharat Range at an insufficient altitude and crashed into the south slope.
Visibility was poor due to overcast conditions.
The approach plates for Kathmandu issued to PIA pilots were also determined to be unclear.
The aircraft crashed at approximately 7300 ft into the side of the 8,250 ft mountain at Bhattedanda, disintegrating on impact.

events.text: The aircraft was cleared for an approach from the south called the Sierra approach.
The aircraft was to then descend in seven steps to 5,800 feet.
The aircraft initiated each step of its descent one step too early.
The aircraft crashed at approximately 7300 ft into the side of the 8,250 ft mountain at Bhattedanda.

title: Libyan Arab Airlines 1103
summary: Flight 1103, a Boeing 727 with 159 people on board, was on approach to Tripoli. At 3161 ft above sea level during approach, the aircraft's tail collided with a Libyan Air Force MiG-23UB right wing and the Boeing disintegrated, killing all 159 passengers and crew. The two MiG-23 crew members ejected and survived. The official investigation concluded the cause was collision with the military aircraft.
probable_cause: Collision with a Libyan Air Force MiG-23 during approach to Tripoli International Airport at 3161 ft altitude.

factors.evidence: the aircraft's tail collided with a Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-23's right wing and disintegrated
official explanation and air accident investigation report both blamed a collision with a Libyan Air Force MiG-23
two air traffic controllers on duty that day, including one civilian controller and one military controller
two air traffic controllers on duty, including one civilian controller still undergoing training under supervision of a military controller

events.text: Flight 1103 took off from Benina International Airport near Benghazi on a domestic flight to Tripoli International Airport.
During approach to Tripoli, the aircraft was at an altitude of 3161 ft above sea level.
The aircraft's tail collided with a Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-23's right wing and disintegrated.
All 159 passengers and crew were killed while the two MiG-23 crew members ejected and survived.

notes: underlying cause of military interception not specified
